message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | 200–1,000 per cell |
| **Muscle cells** (especially cardiac and skeletal muscle) | 500–5,000 per cell |
| **Liver hepatocytes** | 200–1,000 per cell |
| **Epithelial cells** (e.g., intestinal lining) | 50–200 per cell |
| **Stem cells** (low energy demand) | 20–100 per cell |

These numbers are approximate averages; individual cells can have more or fewer mitochondria depending on their metabolic state, developmental stage, and environmental conditions.
